content.transcript: Presenter: Where did they go? And what did they have? Band 1. Father: Ali, where did you go for lunch? Ali: We went to the Sheba Restaurant. Father: And what did you have? Ali: Oh - I had a burger. Presenter: Band 2. Mother: Aisha? Aisha: Yes, Mum? Mother: Aisha, what would you like to drink? Aisha: Can I have an orange juice, please? Mother: Of course. And what would you like to eat? Aisha: Nothing, thanks, Mum. I’m not hungry. Mother: Right. Waiter! Presenter: Band 3. Waiter: Tim? Tim: Oh, hello. Can I have a cheese sandwich, a burger and an apple juice, please? Waiter: A cheese sandwich and a burger and an apple juice? Tim: Yes, please. I’m hungry. Waiter: A cheese sandwich, a burger and an apple juice! Presenter: Band 4. Fatma: Mona, where do you want to go? Salwa: I don’t know. What about you? Where do you want to go? Fatma: Well, I want to go to the Beach Restaurant. Salwa: I don’t. Fatma: Why not? Salwa: I don’t like the Beach Restaurant. I want to go to the Park Restaurant. Fatma: OK. The Park Restaurant. Let me get my bag.

sentences.text: Yesterday, we ___ football in the park. (play)
sentences.explanation: For most regular verbs, we add '-ed' to form the past tense.
If the verb ends in '-e', we just add '-d'.
For short verbs ending in consonant-vowel-consonant, we double the last consonant and add '-ed'.
We add '-ed' to 'walk' to make it past tense.
We add '-ed' to 'visit' to make it past tense.
Since 'live' ends in '-e', we just add '-d'.
We add '-ed' to 'watch' to make it past tense.

activities.title: Pronouncing '-ed' Endings
activities.instruction: Listen carefully! 🎧 Clear your ears and closely! 🎧 Switch on your ears and to the different sounds of the '-ed' ending in these regular past tense verbs. Record yourself saying each word.
activities.compensates: Provides focused, individual pronunciation practice that is difficult to achieve in a full classroom setting.

words.explanation: The '-ed' sounds like /t/ after a 'k' sound.
The '-ed' sounds like /t/ after a 'p' sound.
The '-ed' sounds like /d/ after a vowel sound.
The '-ed' sounds like /d/ after an 'n' sound.
The '-ed' sounds like /ɪd/ after a 't' sound and adds an extra syllable.

activities.title: Choose the Correct Past Tense
activities.instruction: Read the sentence and Take a closer Use your eyes! 🧐 Look closely at the! 📝 Pick the best option for the correct past tense verb to complete it.
activities.compensates: Provides a quick check for understanding of both regular and irregular past tense forms in context.

options.feedback: This is the present tense. We need the past tense for 'last year'.
Correct! 'Moved' is the past tense of 'move'.
This is the present participle form. We need the simple past.

questions.question: Last year, my family ___ to a new house.
questions.explanation: We use the past simple tense to talk about completed actions in the past.

options.feedback: Excellent! 'Heard' is the irregular past tense of 'hear'.
'Hear' is an irregular verb. It does not take '-ed'.
This is the present tense. The sentence is about 'last night'.

questions.question: I ___ a strange noise outside my window last night.
questions.explanation: 'Hear' is an irregular verb. Its past tense form is 'heard'.

options.feedback: This is the present tense. The action happened 'yesterday'.
'Drive' is an irregular verb. It does not take '-ed'.
Correct! 'Drove' is the irregular past tense of 'drive'.

questions.question: Najeeb's father ___ his car to work yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Drive' is an irregular verb. Its past tense form is 'drove'.
